title: Pitts Special (S-2S / S-1S)

sources.title: Pitts S-2S (public knowledge: single-seat aerobatic biplane)
JoyPro function tables MSFS2020/2024 and X-Plane 11/12 (DB/Functions)

intro: The Pitts Special is a small aerobatic biplane, a plane with two wings on each side that is made for stunt flying. The pilot sits in a tiny cockpit with a stick in the centre, and flies the two-seat version from the rear seat. The engine levers are on the left side.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: The compact panel in front of the pilot.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: A small, compact panel with the few instruments that an aerobatic plane needs: speed, height, load, engine speed and engine health.
panels.context: The plane is made for stunt flying, so there are few dials, and the pilot flies mostly by looking outside.

controls.name: Airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane moves through the air.
controls.context: The pilot watches it on take-off, landing and in stunts.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows the height of the plane above sea level.
controls.context: The pilot keeps a safe height for the stunts.

controls.name: G-meter
controls.text: This dial shows the load factor, how strongly the pilot is pushed into the seat during turns and pulls. 1 is the normal pull of gravity.
controls.context: It shows how hard the pilot is pulling the plane in stunts.

controls.name: Tachometer
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the engine turns, in revolutions per minute (RPM).
controls.context: The engine speed tells the pilot how much power the engine gives.

controls.name: Manifold pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows how hard air is pushed into the engine, which tells how much power it makes.
controls.context: The pilot uses it together with the propeller lever to set the power.

controls.name: Oil temperature / pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature and the pressure of the engine oil.
controls.context: Oil keeps the engine parts from wearing out; the pilot checks it after starting.

controls.name: Magneto switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The magnetos are off and the engine stops.

positions.name: BOTH
positions.text: Both magnetos work, the normal setting for flight.

controls.text: This switch turns the magnetos on. Magnetos are small generators that make the sparks for the engine, and there are two for safety.
controls.context: The pilot sets it to BOTH for normal flight.

areas.name: Left side: engine levers and trim
areas.text: The left side of the cockpit with the engine levers, the trim and the fuel control.

panels.name: Left side console
panels.text: The engine levers, the trim and the fuel control on the left side of the pilot.
panels.context: The pilot's left hand rests on the throttle while the right hand holds the stick.

controls.name: Throttle lever
controls.text: This lever sets how much power the engine gives. Pushing it forward gives more power.
controls.context: The pilot pushes it forward for take-off.

controls.name: Propeller lever
controls.text: This lever sets the propeller speed, which means how sharply the blades bite the air.
controls.context: The pilot sets it to match the power wanted from the engine.

controls.name: Mixture lever
controls.text: This lever sets how much fuel is mixed with the air, from rich (more fuel) to lean and cut-off, which stops the engine.
controls.context: The pilot makes the mixture leaner at higher altitudes, where the air is thinner.

controls.name: Elevator trim lever
controls.text: This small lever trims the nose up or down. Trim removes the steady push on the stick.
controls.context: The pilot uses it after changing speed.

controls.name: Fuel selector / pump
controls.text: This control selects the fuel supply to the engine and the fuel pump, which helps to move the fuel.
controls.context: It is part of the fuel system of the engine.

areas.name: Control stick and pedals
areas.text: The controls the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.

panels.name: Control stick and pedals
panels.text: The controls the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.
panels.context: The Pitts reacts quickly to small movements of the stick.

controls.name: Control stick
controls.text: Pushing the stick forward points the nose down, pulling it back points it up. Moving it sideways rolls the plane left or right, with ailerons on both wings.
controls.context: A biplane has two wings on each side, and ailerons on all of them make it roll very fast.

controls.name: Rudder pedals
controls.text: The pedals move the rudder on the tail to point the nose left or right. The tops of the pedals are the toe brakes for the left and right wheels.
controls.context: On the ground the brakes are used with the feet.
